dialogue.user: Hi there! I'm looking for a book that fits my preferences. I'm interested in books with advice and I want to spend between $15 and $30. Do you have any recommendations?
dialogue.agent:
I found a few books that match your criteria. Here are the details:

1. **"The Candy In My Pocket: The Wild and Crazy Life of a Type 1 Diabetic"**
   - Price: $25.95
   - Average Rating: 5.0
   - Number of Reviews: 11
   - Description: Review "I laughed out loud at every story. John 's triumph over medical adversity is enormously uplifting. He chooses joy, happiness and unwavering positivity in his quest to live life on his own terms. I have never met a person with more energy and pathological optimism. \" Cynthia Rowley, global fashion and home accessories designer. \" John has a talent for storytelling and writing as well as for design, but the most important part of this memoir is his amazing energy and determination to live hurdles of the debilitating disease type 1 diabetes! He enjoys a full life gathering fabulous, famous and adventurous friends, and gives back to many far more than he takes. He never looks back, always forward choosing to be happy and fully engaged while hiding his scars and physically damaged parts with Versace!\" Holly Hunt, founder of the luxury home furnishings and design brand \"The well-informed individual knows type 1 diabetes is a disease of blood vessels (eye, kidney, brain, heart, extremities). Actually, though, it is a disease of people and Mr. Wiltgen gives us in an informative, often entertaining, account how he spent much of his life learning to manage this debilitating disease - or perhaps more correctly, how diabetes mellitus has managed much of his life.\" Dr. David Mehlman, Associate Professor, Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine \"The Candy in my Pocket is a great example of how the most interesting people are not those with problems but those who overcome them. John Wiltgen is one such person. A line from his memoir, \"a complex synthesis of standards, attractions, sensations, lust, love and fantasy\" describes not only design but also John Robert Wiltgen. The Candy in My Pocket, the story of a boy who first learned he had type 1 diabetes at age 8 but didn't allow this debilitating disease to affect the man he is today, is truly one of this award-winning designer's best accomplishments.\" Gera-Lind Kolarik, author Freed to Kill, I Am Cain, Prisoners of Fear \"This book is a wonderful and entertaining read. It accurately depicts the difficulties that type 1 diabetics must face. All of which John Wiltgen handles with humor and style.\" Dr . Jennifer Lee, Clinical Assistant Professor, Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, Board certified American Board of Internal Medicine (Infectious Disease and Internal Medicine) About the Author John Robert Wiltgen started writing as soon as his mother bought him a used Underwood typewriter at a garage sale. During middle school he was editor of the school newspaper. He graduated high school in 3 years studying art, literature, creative writing and theater. When he was 17, he was the manager of the Midwest region's model store for the Glidden Paint company while he studied interior design in the evenings despite his mother's pleas he should be an accountant. \"You can always get a job as an accountant,\" she argued. To no one's surprise he didn't take her advice. He's a Leo. Instead, he quit his lucrative job at the paint store to attend design school full-time. After a brief stint at Ray Vogue School of Design, the headmaster asked him to clean out his locker, stop paying his monthly tuition installments and never return. He was 18 years old when he embarked on his career as a residential designer and never looked back. It's nearly impossible to build a luxury design firm while living in the moldy basement of your parent's modest suburban home. The challenge grew significantly when he lost his sight a short time later. After all, who wants to hire a blind decorator? At 22 John was diagnosed with retinopathy-damage to the retina caused by abnormal blood flow-a complication of diabetes. And though diabetic retinopathy is the leading cause of blindness in working-aged people it did not stop John from building his brand as a luxury home design professional. Despite a four-year period of blindness, followed by many other complications of type 1 diabetes, John continued to grow his residential design firm. He obsessed over making his client's worlds beautiful taking him across North America and halfway around the world-from Chicago's Gold Coast to Africa's Ivory Coast. His firm's name is synonymous with its reputation for excellence and superior quality in design, styling, and craftsmanship."

2. **"The 24 (Thoughts for my sons)"**
   - Price: $15.99
   - Average Rating: 5.0
   - Number of Reviews: 2
   - Description: N/A

dialogue.user: Thank you for the recommendations! The first book, "The Candy In My Pocket: The Wild and Crazy Life of a Type 1 Diabetic," seems quite interesting. The reviews mention it's uplifting and entertaining, which is great. However, I'm a bit concerned about the number of reviews. Only 11 reviews might not give a full picture of the book's quality. What do you think about the number of reviews for this book? Also, could you tell me more about the second book, "The 24 (Thoughts for my sons)"? It has a perfect rating, but there are only 2 reviews. How detailed are those reviews?
dialogue.agent:
Here are the top reviews for the books you're interested in:

1. **"The Candy In My Pocket: The Wild and Crazy Life of a Type 1 Diabetic"**
   - **Review 1**:
     - Title: "A story of a surviver and a creator who is living life his way!"
     - Rating: 5.0
     - Text: "Here is a book I want you to read…it’s a story about a creator…a lesson in self awareness and self preservation…a travelogue…anything but your usual memoir, it’s a very powerful story. There is SO much information included that I read it twice, I don’t remember doing that before. I want to share the joie de vivre John has for survival…for life! Sharing his incredible story is a journey more fiction than fact but guess what…it is the story of his life and one we can all learn from. It’s inspirational…it’s inspiring…it should be depressing it is anything but…it’s a MUST read!!!! Okay let’s get to the unbelievable story John tells us. The song, “I’m Still Here” from Follies should be the subtitle of this amazing life. John begins at the beginning…his childhood, filled with adventure which continues to this day. He was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes at the age of 8 a fact he managed to keep hidden much of his life. As a child and a teenager he was quite rebellious, in a fun way, he started working while in high school at a paint company where he rose to an executive positions, still in his teens, he never told anyone his age…the writing was on the wall for his future career. He lived in a Chicago suburb and, as an under age teen, loved disco dancing and would come to Chicago with his close friends to frequent the major discos such as FACES (I spent many an evening there!). He and his friends would practice for hours in his basement apartment in his parents home. They were so good they became the dance floor stars…in my minds eye I picture John Travolta! The book doesn’t sugar coat (sorry, I shouldn’t mention sugar but it seemed appropriate!) when John describes his ongoing battle with the unbelievable complications of Type 1 Diabetes. He has had so many that it could read like a horror story, instead it is done in such a straightforward positive way that you know he hasn’t and won’t let anything stop him from living life fully! He presents his many, many, many challenges along side his interests, cars for an example, travel, the arts and his love for them, his philanthropic endeavors, his love for family and friends and, of course, his extraordinary interior design business. Speaking of family…how many can say that all members of their family would be a match if you needed a kidney and your mother said, no, I’m donating mine…talk about a mother’s love! John’s support team through the years has sustained him along with his feeling of what’s next in life and always seeking a cure and an end to this life threatening disease. In conclusion what are my take aways from this beautifully written story of a survivor…so many things but let me narrow it down. John tackles each challenge in his fight against this dreadful disease…one day at a time, one horrific devastating outcome…one day at a time with grit, determination and, yes, humor. What should be a depressing book is anything but because of the author’s joie de vivre and positive attitude. You will learn so much about Type 1 Diabetes and be inspired to join the fight to find a cure as well as how to handle your own day to day issues. My last words…get the book you won’t be disappointed and by reading it you will be delighted to welcome John as a new fascinating multi-layered friend."
   - **Review 2**:
     - Title: "LIVING life to the fullest!"
     - Rating: 5.0
     - Text: "For those of us fortunate enough to live a healthy life, this biography may be hard to relate to. I found it almost impossible to believe all the complications of type 1 diabetes John Robert Wiltgen has survived. It’s amazing. What an inspiration to anyone. You do not have to be sick to appreciate the strength and positive energy this man possesses. He says his career in design enabled him to live life to the fullest. After reading The Candy in My Pocket I want to be a designer."
   - **Review 3**:
     - Title: "Not matter what life hands you never give up hope"
     - Rating: 5.0
     - Text: "This story is the essence of a man accepting the fears and restrictions of diabetes so he could live life to the fullest. With extraordinary skill he engaged in the world of interior design resulting in a stellar 40-year practice. Despite a long list of diabetes related complications, he succeeded in attracting an extensive portfolio of clients. His irreverent sense of humor and tear-jerking experiences govern his ongoing commitment to Life. Although this fascinating book is a quick read there is a lot in it to digest. I will definitely read it again. Marty Kaprelian"

2. **"The 24 (Thoughts for my sons)"**
   - **Review 1**:
     - Title: "Advice from a Father to his Sons to carry throughout their lives"
     - Rating: 5.0
     - Text: "The author, a loving caring father, has chosen to create poems to leave for his sons to carry with them throughout their lives. It gives his sons a continuation of what he has tried to instill in them long after they have left the nest. This book can be appropriate for other fathers to give to their sons."
   - **Review 2**:
     - Title: "A great book for everyone"
     - Rating: 5.0
     - Text: "In Gary Johnson's debut book \"The 24 Thoughts For My Son\" he embarks on a journey of putting down a collection of thoughts, knowledge and advice for his sons via poetry with surprising results. The book is perfect for today's fast paced environment. It isn't comprised of hours and hours of writings but it is composed of short precise advise. It exceeded all of my expectations and left me speechless(which in itself is a miracle). As a father it seemed as though his thoughts were my thoughts and I felt a deep connection from the 1st poem to the last poem. The book contains knowledge that I would not only want to share with my son (I purchased an additional book for him) but knowledge that I would want to share with everyone."

These reviews should give you a better idea of what to expect from each book.

He and his friends would practice for hours in his basement apartment in his parents home. They were so good they became the dance floor stars…in my minds eye I picture John Travolta!

The book doesn’t sugar coat (sorry, I shouldn’t mention sugar but it seemed appropriate!) when John describes his ongoing battle with the unbelievable complications of Type 1 Diabetes. He has had so many that it could read like a horror story, instead it is done in such a straightforward positive way that you know he hasn’t and won’t let anything stop him from living life fully! He presents his many, many, many challenges along side his interests, cars for an example, travel, the arts and his love for them, his philanthropic endeavors, his love for family and friends and, of course, his extraordinary interior design business.

Speaking of family…how many can say that all members of their family would be a match if you needed a kidney and your mother said, no, I’m donating mine…talk about a mother’s love! John’s support team through the years has sustained him along with his feeling of what’s next in life and always seeking a cure and an end to this life threatening disease.

In conclusion what are my take aways from this beautifully written story of a survivor…..so many things but let me narrow it down. John tackles each challenge in his fight against this dreadful disease…one day at a time, one horrific devastating outcome…one day at a time with grit, determination and, yes, humor. What should be a depressing book is anything but because of the author’s joie de vivre and positive attitude. You will learn so much about Type 1 Diabetes and be inspired to join the fight to find a cure as well as how to handle your own day to day issues. My last words….get the book you won’t be disappointed and by reading it you will be delighted to welcome John as a new fascinating multi-layered friend.

top_reviews.title: LIVING life to the fullest !
top_reviews.text: For those of us fortunate enough to live a healthy life, this biography may be hard to relate to. I found it almost impossible to believe all the complications of type 1 diabetes John Robert Wiltgen has survived. It’s amazing. What an inspiration to anyone. You do not have to be sick to appreciate the strength and positive energy this man possesses. He says his career in design enabled him to live life to the fullest. After reading The Candy in My Pocket I want to be a designer.

top_reviews.title: Not matter what life hands you never give up hope
top_reviews.text:
This story is the essence of a man accepting the fears and restrictions of diabetes so he could live life to the fullest. With extraordinary skill he engaged in the world of interior design resulting in a stellar 40-year practice. Despite a long list of diabetes related complications, he succeeded in attracting an extensive portfolio of clients. His irreverent sense of humor and tear-jerking experiences govern his ongoing commitment to Life. Although this fascinating book is a quick read there is a lot in it to digest. I will definitely read it again.

Marty Kaprelian

top_reviews.title: Advice from a Father to his Sons to carry throughout their lives
top_reviews.text: The author, a loving caring  father, has chosen to create poems to leave for  his sons to carry with them throughout their lives.  It gives his sons a continuation of what he has tried to instill in them long after they have left the nest.  This book  can be appropriate for other fathers to  give to their sons.

top_reviews.title: A great book for everyone
top_reviews.text: In Gary Johnson's debut book "The 24 Thoughts For My Son" he embarks on a journey of putting down a collection of thoughts, knowledge and advice for his sons via poetry with surprising results. The book is perfect for today's fast paced environment.  It isn't comprised of hours and hours of writings but it is composed of short  precise advise. It exceeded all of my expectations and left me speechless(which in itself is a miracle). As a father it seemed as though his thoughts were my thoughts and I felt a deep connection from the 1st poem to the last poem. The book contains knowledge that I would not only want to share with my son (I purchased an additional book for him) but knowledge that I would want to share with everyone.

products.title: The Candy In My Pocket: The Wild and Crazy Life of a Type 1 Diabetic
products.description: Review "I laughed out loud at every story. John 's triumph over medical adversity is enormously uplifting. " Cynthia Rowley, global fashion and home accessories designer. " John has a talent for storytelling and writing as well as for design, but the most important part of this memoir is his amazing energy and determination to live hurdles of the debilitating disease type 1 diabetes! He enjoys a full life gathering fabulous, famous and adventurous friends, and gives back to many far more than he takes. He never looks back, always forward choosing to be happy and fully engaged while hiding his scars and physically damaged parts with Versace!" Holly Hunt, founder of the luxury home furnishings and design brand "The well-informed individual knows type 1 diabetes is a disease of blood vessels (eye, kidney, brain, heart, extremities). Actually, though, it is a disease of people and Mr. Wiltgen gives us in an informative, often entertaining, account how he spent much of his life learning to manage this debilitating disease - or perhaps more correctly, how diabetes mellitus has managed much of his life." Dr. David Mehlman, Associate Professor, Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine "The Candy in my Pocket is a great example of how the most interesting people are not those with problems but those who overcome them. John Wiltgen is one such person. A line from his memoir, "a complex synthesis of standards, attractions, sensations, lust, love and fantasy" describes not only design but also John Robert Wiltgen. The Candy in My Pocket, the story of a boy who first learned he had type 1 diabetes at age 8 but didn't allow this debilitating disease to affect the man he is today, is truly one of this award-winning designer's best accomplishments." Gera-Lind Kolarik, author Freed to Kill, I Am Cain, Prisoners of Fear "This book is a wonderful and entertaining read. It accurately depicts the difficulties that type 1 diabetics must face. All of which John Wiltgen handles with humor and style." Dr . Jennifer Lee, Clinical Assistant Professor, Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, Board certified American Board of Internal Medicine (Infectious Disease and Internal Medicine) About the Author John Robert Wiltgen started writing as soon as his mother bought him a used Underwood typewriter at a garage sale. During middle school he was editor of the school newspaper. He graduated high school in 3 years studying art, literature, creative writing and theater. When he was 17, he was the manager of the Midwest region's model store for the Glidden Paint company while he studied interior design in the evenings despite his mother's pleas he should be an accountant. "You can always get a job as an accountant," she argued. To no one's surprise he didn't take her advice. He's a Leo. Instead, he quit his lucrative job at the paint store to attend design school full-time. After a brief stint at Ray Vogue School of Design, the headmaster asked him to clean out his locker, stop paying his monthly tuition installments and never return. He was 18 years old when he embarked on his career as a residential designer and never looked back. It's nearly impossible to build a luxury design firm while living in the moldy basement of your parent's modest suburban home. The challenge grew significantly when he lost his sight a short time later. After all, who wants to hire a blind decorator? At 22 John was diagnosed with retinopathy-damage to the retina caused by abnormal blood flow-a complication of diabetes. And though diabetic retinopathy is the leading cause of blindness in working-aged people it did not stop John from building his brand as a luxury home design professional. Despite a four-year period of blindness, followed by many other complications of type 1 diabetes, John continued to grow his residential design firm. He obsessed over making his client's worlds beautiful taking him across North America and halfway around the world-from Chicago's Gold Coast to Africa's Ivory Coast. His firm's name is synonymous with its reputation for excellence and superior quality in design, styling, and craftsmanship.
